territorial_scope.description: Applies in Denmark to operators and owners of data centres with installed IT power of 500 kW or more; individual decisions and orders under § 9 address specific operators.

evidence.quote: Denne bekendtgørelse vedrører regler om indberetning og offentliggørelse af oplysninger vedrørende datacentres energimæssige ydeevne.

summary.short: Danish executive order (BEK nr. 926 of 2024) requiring operators of data centres with at least 500 kW installed IT power to report energy, water and related indicators to the European data centre database, supervised by the Danish Energy Agency; in force from 1 September 2024.
summary.long: Danish executive order (BEK nr. 926 of 9 July 2024), issued under the Energy Efficiency Act and in force from 1 September 2024 (§ 12). Operators of data centres with installed IT power of 500 kW or more must report to the European data centre database (§§ 3-4), first by 15 September 2024 and then by 15 May each year. Reported data covers name, owner, commissioning date, location, floor area, installed power, data traffic, stored data and the indicators in Annexes I and II, including energy, water, renewable energy, heat reuse and IT capacity. Facilities used solely for defence and civil protection are exempt (§ 3(2)). Information protected by trade-secret or confidentiality rules may be exempted from publication (§ 5(2)), and exemption documentation may be submitted to the Danish Energy Agency for approval (§ 6(2)). The agency supervises compliance and may issue orders with a deadline (§§ 8-9). Non-compliance, false reporting or failure to obey an order is punishable by fines, and companies may face criminal liability (§ 10). Decisions may be appealed to the Energy Appeals Board within four weeks, and to courts only after the final administrative decision (§ 11). The order implements parts of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 and reproduces Annexes I-IV of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, which the text says applies directly in each Member State.

notes: Internal inconsistencies: (1) § 3 sets the reporting threshold at 500 kW installed IT load, while Bilag 4 lists size categories starting at 100 kW ('meget lille datacenter: 100-500 kW'). (2) Bilag 5 heads the reproduced EU act as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1363, while the preamble, § 2 and the other annex headers cite 2024/1364. (3) Bilag 2 defines EIT in kWh, but Bilag 3(b) says EIT is 'udtrykkes i MWh' for the WUE formula. (4) § 11 lists § 10 among the provisions whose decisions may be appealed to the Energy Appeals Board, although § 10 is a criminal sanction provision. Other points: Figures 1 to 3 referred to in Bilag 2 and 3 are not reproduced. § 10 states no fine amount. The enabling act is cited as amended by Act 1555 of 12 December 2023, and that amendment is not in the document. target_instrument_id is an empty string throughout because no registry IDs were supplied.
